paper text.text:
\begin{lemma}\label{r1:exterior-faces}
In a torus embedding of $\Psi_3$, let $\mathcal N$ be a closed regular
neighborhood of $\Psi_3$. If $\mathcal N$ has genus one and a face meets
$b,c,d,e$, that face is a disk with attachment sequence
$a,b,a,d,a,c,a,e$, up to cyclic shift and reversal, and the other
two faces have attachment sequences $bc,de$. If $\mathcal N$ has genus zero, any face
meeting $b,c,d,e$ is an annulus with attachment sequences $bc\mid de$, and
the other three faces are disks with attachment sequences $axay$, $ax'$ and
$ay'$, where $\{x,x'\}=\{b,c\}$ and $\{y,y'\}=\{d,e\}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each of the $96$ rotation systems of $\Psi_3$, the table in~\supp{R6} gives the attachments in order along each facial walk. No rotation system of genus zero has a face containing all four of $b,c,d,e$ in its boundary walk. The only pair of facial walks in any rotation system of genus zero whose union contains all four has attachment sequences $bc,de$. Thus, by Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}, a face meeting all four in a torus embedding with this rotation must be an annulus with attachment sequences $bc\mid de$. The other three facial walks of such a rotation have attachment sequences $axay$, $ax'$ and $ay'$, and bound disks by the same lemma. Of the genus-one rotations, the only facial attachment sequence containing all four is $abadacae$, up to cyclic shift and reversal. The other two faces have attachment sequences $bc,de$.

what: Every rotation system of Psi_3. Attachments a, b, c, d, e; twins omitted.
how to read: At each vertex, 'cyclic orders' lists the neighbor orders lexicographically, starting each order with the least neighbor. Rotation systems are numbered from 0 in the order of 'vertices', with the last vertex varying fastest. The entry rows[i] indexes 'distinct rows' for rotation system i. Each row gives the genus (2 - V + E - F)/2 and the sorted attachment sequences of the facial walks. After u->v a walk takes v->w, where w follows u at v. A sequence records every visit to an attachment, starting at the least cyclic shift and keeping the walk direction. For claims up to reversal, take the least cyclic shift of either direction.

graphs.row format: [genus, attachment sequences of the facial walks]

claims.statement: There are 6 * 2^4 = 96 rotations; a rotation with f facial walks has genus (5 - f)/2.
In genus one, a walk containing b, c, d, e has sequence a,b,a,d,a,c,a,e up to cyclic shift and reversal, and the other two walks have sequences bc, de.
In genus zero, the sequences are abad, ac, ae, bc, de, up to interchanging b, c and interchanging d, e; no single walk meets b, c, d, e, and the only pair that does is bc, de.
